meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'where', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А где машинка? Где моя машинка?
examples.trans: Hey, where's the toy car? Where's my toy car?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common masculine noun meaning 'tartare' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый тартар.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new tartare.

meanings.note: Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'boy' in everyday Russian.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('first').

examples.text: Ты не понимаешь с первого раза?
examples.trans: You don't understand the first time?

examples.text: Ты что, с первого раза не понимаешь?
examples.trans: What, you don't understand the first time?

выйти.gloss: to go out, to get out

meanings.en: to go out, to get out
meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go out, to get out', paired with 'выходить'.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks.

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Common feminine noun meaning 'panic' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Среди испуганных пассажиров началась ужасная паника.
examples.trans: Among frightened passengers a terrible panic began.
See, the panic disappears by itself.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'должать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to continue', paired with 'продолжить'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to work', paired with 'поработать'.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'go, walk', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: That's why I'm running for a second term.

examples.text: А ты иди на биржу труда. Там есть работа.
examples.trans: You go to the job centre. There's work there.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

examples.text: Мы сюда зачем прилетели? Я сразу сказал: с ним ничего не получится.
examples.trans: What did we even fly out here for? I said from the start: nothing will come of it with him.
Why did you even come here? Empty-handed!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'могать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to help', paired with 'помочь'.

examples.text: Так, операцию продолжаем. Михаил Михайлович, помогайте Лаврову.
examples.trans: Right, the operation goes on. Mikhail Mikhailovich, give Lavrov your help.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'суда'). Common feminine noun meaning 'dishes, tableware, crockery' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Get up and go wash the dishes!
Clean tableware is on the table.

examples.text: Юля, встала и пошла мыть посуду!
examples.trans: Yulia, get up and go wash the dishes!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'how; as', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'time, occasion' in everyday Russian.

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'время').

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'at, by; (у меня) I have', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: There are plenty of people there.

examples.text: А почему мой шашлык никто не ест? Мяса полно!
examples.trans: And why is nobody eating my shashlik? There's plenty of meat!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'order' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я делаю всё точно по вашему заказу.
examples.trans: I do everything exactly according to your order.
In the kitchen they are preparing this order.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'everything, all; that's it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go (by vehicle), to set off
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to set off', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cold, chilly; distant').

examples.trans: You are a good woman. Cold.

examples.text: Лёня быстро бросил в холодную воду поддон.
examples.trans: Lyonya quickly threw a wooden pallet into cold water.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'sauce' (ultimately from Latin 'salsa', salted seasoning).

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('hot').

examples.trans: Careful, the cup is very hot.

examples.text: Аркаша, держи горячий чай. И бутерброд с вареньем ешь.
examples.trans: Arkasha, here's some hot tea. And eat a jam sandwich.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'pepper' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

examples.text: Попробуй! Лук, соль, перец — и всё.
examples.trans: Try it! Onion, salt, pepper — and that's all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'пара'). Common feminine noun meaning 'rush, mess, chaos' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: A rush began in the kitchen.
The rush does not happen in the kitchen.

examples.text: Настоящая запара всегда только в голове!
examples.trans: The real rush is always only in your head!
